facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s with a history of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
The lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
A well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque, 15 × 12 cm, was seen over the right side of the anterior chest wall around her operation scar
Scattered within the erythema were multiple palpable small nodules
Negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
Right mastectomy scar with a large well-defined area of erythema and multiple, scattered small nodules
Nearly complete remission of skin lesions after treatment

concepts.why: The patient's history of breast cancer and the presence of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast, which did not respond to initial topical treatments, suggest a diagnosis of inflammatory breast cancer.

The patient's history of breast cancer and the presence of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast, which did not respond to initial topical treatments, suggest a diagnosis of locoregional breast cancer recurrence.

The patient's history of radiation therapy and the presence of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast suggest a diagnosis of radiation dermatitis.

The patient's history of breast cancer and the presence of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast, which did not respond to initial topical treatments, suggest a diagnosis of cutaneous metastasis.
The patient's skin biopsy was negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, which is consistent with triple-negative breast cancer.

rationales.F01: History of breast cancer increases the likelihood of locoregional recurrence.
rationales.F02: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules is suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer or cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F04: Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque with multiple palpable small nodules is highly suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer or cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F05: Multiple palpable small nodules within the erythema are highly suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer or cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F06: Negative ER, PR, and HER2 status is characteristic of triple-negative breast cancer.
rationales.F07: Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels is diagnostic of cutaneous metastasis or inflammatory breast cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, as seen in the skin biopsy, strongly supports cutaneous metastasis, which is a direct sign of cancer spread to the skin.
